channel.title: [podly] The AI Daily Brief: Artificial Intelligence News and Analysis
channel.description: A daily news analysis show on all things artificial intelligence. NLW looks at AI from multiple angles, from the explosion of creativity brought on by new tools like Midjourney and ChatGPT to the potential disruptions to work and industries as we know them to the great philosophical, ethical and practical questions of advanced general intelligence, alignment and x-risk.

item.title: What Anthropic’s IPO Filing Reveals
item.ns0:encoded:
Explosive revenue growth, $132 billion in cash, and hundreds of billions in compute commitments. NLW breaks down what Anthropic’s IPO filing reveals about its business—and the future growth needed to justify its enormous bets. In the headlines: OpenAI’s scientific breakthroughs, GPT-6.1 Terra’s computer-use capabilities, and a Chinese model’s unexpected network activity sparks a security debate.

item.title: Introducing How We Got Here -- NLW's new podcast
item.ns0:encoded:
NLW's new show How We Got Here launched today. It's a weekly deep dive into how today's biggest stories came to be, made for the topics that have too much backstory to fit into the AI Daily Brief. This is the first five minutes of Episode 1, How Tech Lost America, about how tech went from America's most trusted industry to a symbol of people's anxieties about wealth and power.

item.title: How I'm Actually Using AI Right Now (Including Claude Duet)
item.ns0:encoded:
Claude Duet's launch is an opportunity to take stock of how I'm actually using AI today. From strategy and research to coding, content creation and data analysis, I break down my current AI stack and which models work best for which tasks. Then, a comparison of ChatGPT Dots and Claude Duet, and why proactive personal agents might finally be finding their place in my workflow.

item.title: How AI Is Changing What Work Means
item.ns0:encoded:
Why is a financial research firm using AI to design proteins that target scorpion venom? Because AI is changing what work means—and what businesses are capable of doing. Citrini Research’s unexpected experiment opens up bigger questions about who gets to do science, whether AI labs will compete with their customers, and how far companies can push beyond their traditional expertise. In the headlines: Muse hits 10 million US downloads, Gemini gets more personal in Android Auto, and Anthropic’s financial disclosures spark fresh valuation debates.

item.title: Why AI Companies Are Betting Personality Beats Intelligence
item.ns0:encoded:
As AI models become more capable, personality is becoming a competitive battleground. From the GPT-4o backlash to Meta’s Muse and ChatGPT’s Dots, NLW explores why how an AI feels to use could increasingly determine which products win—and which models work best for different tasks.
